name: counter_queue
description: The holder's answer: when the armed holder can act it queues its own default attack (Chr+0x6c6) at the attacker as a reaction (kind 1, priority 0); the armed byte is cleared either way.

function.signature: int queue_counter(int attackerId, Chr *attacker, int holderId, Chr *holder)

harness.note: the real machine code of the function in an x86-32 emulator; the three status-flag tables read from the exe memory; queue inserts hooked

notes: in.holder is the holder's Chr fields the call reads (Can-act: in-battle, Petrified, permanent word, Sleep counter, extra word) plus Chr+0x6c6 (defAtk) and the armed byte; every other field is 0.

out.record is the queued action record decoded: actor byte, the command count, the command (u16 at +8), the target mask (u32 at +0x10) and the call's arguments [priority, kind, attacker id]; absent when nothing was queued. The attacker's Chr+0x6dd write is presentation only and not carried.
